paragraphs: Cincinnati Reds won. LyDia's model favored the other side.

Rhett Lowder (No clear pitching-plan edge) was LyDia's favored starter by pitcher score, but David Peterson actually pitched better tonight: 5.0 IP, 2 ER (3.60 ERA) against 5.0 IP, 3 ER (5.40 ERA). The edge did not show up in this game.
The Cincinnati Reds bullpen was not flagged pregame, but it had a night worth noting: 5 earned runs allowed over 4.0 relief innings (11.25 ERA) — quietly worse than the pregame read implied.

The Chicago Cubs bullpen was not flagged pregame, but it had a night worth noting: 6 earned runs allowed over 4.0 relief innings (13.50 ERA) — quietly worse than the pregame read implied. Note: 2 of the runs charged to the Chicago Cubs pitching staff overall were unearned — not something the bullpen's stuff should be blamed for.
Cincinnati Reds scored 10, 7.1 more than the 2.9 pregame projection.
Chicago Cubs scored 8, 3.8 more than the 4.2 pregame projection.

Likely driver: the Chicago Cubs bullpen allowed 6 earned runs over 4.0 relief innings (13.50 ERA), which was not flagged pregame but showed up anyway, and Cincinnati Reds's offense scored 7.1 more runs than projected.
